summary: ```markdown # CLO Technique Workshop - Making Elastic Bands (Three-Layer Structure) ## Introduction Hello everyone! Today, I will teach you how to make a three-layer structure elastic band. You can see that the embedded waist plate is a double-layer structure. First, we will delete one of them and then use the Cologne method to make it more convenient. ## Creating the Elastic Band Plate We will now create the elastic band plate. If there is a process list, it can be created according to the data on the process list. If not, we can refer to the waist value of the model to create it. 1. **Open the Virtual Model Editor**: - Find the waist value. - You can look at the lower dimension value by dragging the measurement line to find the position where the half skirt is naturally worn. - You should see that the dimension is about 620 mm. 2. **Use the Shape Tool**: - Create the elastic band plate. - The width needs to be larger than the waist reference value mentioned earlier, accounting for some loose amounts. - The height should be the same as the waist belt. 3. **Sewing Lines**: - Since there are two lines on the waist belt, they need to be sewn. - Create two internal lines for the elastic band plate. 4. **Generate Internal Lines**: - Use the edit version tool to select the upper and lower two lines, then right-click to generate internal lines between them. - Use the shortcut key to switch to the Cologne outline and select the baseline, returning to the Cologne as the internal line. ## Arranging Templates Now let's arrange the waist and elastic band templates. 1. **Adjust Template Points**: - Use the shortcut key SHIFT + F to open the adjustments point. - Pre-fold the two templates and swap to world coordinates to locate the ball, making it convenient in any perspective. - Move the template and select the two templates to align together at the arrangement points of the Medicare waist. 2. **Muscle Alignment**: - Shake our muscles to hold against the side to create uniformness. - This is exactly what the default scale adjustment project aims to achieve. 3. **Shoulder Strap Adjustments**: - At this time, the back of the waist plate overlaps with the back of the waist plate, so adjust the shoulder strap in the attribute editor to avoid overlap. - Similarly, the shoulder strap of the loose belt can be appropriately narrowed. - Adjust the height of the two plates as needed before sewing them together. ## Sewing and Simulation 1. **Sew the Plate**: - Remember to change the lining of the overlapping plate to the lining of the outside of the plate. - Use the shortcut key of the single引 code to change the lining. 2. **Check the Sewing Line**: - In the 3D window, check the sewing line to confirm that there are no wrong or missing stitches. 3. **Simulation Preparation**: - If you directly open the simulation, the waist of the skirt may fall down. - Use Ctrl + Z to retract any changes. 4. **Applying Materials**: - Before running the simulation, apply the correct material to the loose belt plate by adding a new piece of fabric. - Find the material in the canvas window, where there is a loose belt file under the material category. - There are two pieces of loose belt material: one needle and one shrink. Here, we choose to use the needle loose belt and drag it to the fabric to replace it. 5. **Physical Attributes**: - In the attribute editor below, check the physical attribute details of the loose belt. - After opening the simulation again, the skirt should now fit normally on the model, with no wrinkle details at the waist. ## Final Adjustments 1. **Middle Plate Adjustments**: - Select the middle plate and reduce the particle diameter of the two plates to 5. - Simulate again to observe the wrinkle details. 2. **Hiding the Inner Layer**: - Shift + A to hide the model. - Next, make the waist plate of the inner layer by selecting the outer layer of the plate and right-clicking. - Use Ctrl to go to the inside of the layer and change the editing sewing line tool. - After selecting the frame, delete all the sewing lines of this plate. 3. **Reassigning Sewing Lines**: - Change the sewing line to the sewing line of the loose belt plate in the middle. - Remember to sew the two ends of the plate. ## Conclusion 1. **Edge Adjustments**: - Select the middle plate and right-click on the 3D window to add it to the inside. - Open the simulation and apply the corresponding fabric to the skirt. - Simulate again, and you will notice the white loose belt showing on the edge. 2. **Finalizing the Layers**: - To hide this effect, first delete all the sewing lines on the edge of the plate and switch to the texture surface display. - You may see that the plate is upside down at this point; turn over the surface. - Sew the edges of the two waist plates together, paying attention to the sewing direction. 3. **Simulation Check**: - You can sew before turning over the surface. - Select these two sewing lines and change the folding angle to 0 degrees. - Open the simulation again, and you will see that because the two plates are sewn together directly, the loose belt plate in the middle layer can be hidden. - Because the two plates are facing each other, change the folding angle of the sewing line to 0 degrees. 4. **Final Touches**: - To make the fold more delicate, select the edge line of the middle plate and draw it. - Simulate again to stabilize. The three-layer structure of the loose belt is now finished! Finally, use a tool to improve the quality of clothing to optimize the clothing effect. Thank you for watching, and see you in the next video! ```
